title: SOC2 Control Mapping Discrepancy Across Policy Versions During Audit
scenario_text:
**Vanta — SOC2 Type II Audit Prep Dashboard (Audit period: Jul 2025 - Jun 2026)**
Control CC-7.2: 'Vulnerability Management — Critical vulnerabilities are remediated within 14 days of identification.'
Status: Evidence Gap | Auditor Note (Jun 12, 2026): 'Observed 3 instances where critical vulns exceeded 14-day SLA. Requesting management response.'

**Confluence — Security Policy SP-012: Vulnerability Management (v4.0, effective Apr 2026)**
Section 5.1: 'Critical vulnerabilities (CVSS >= 9.0) must be remediated within 14 calendar days.'
Section 5.4: 'Exceptions require CISO approval documented in Jira with risk acceptance rationale.'
[Page history: v3.1 (effective Jan 2025) stated: 'Critical vulnerabilities must be remediated within 30 calendar days. High vulnerabilities within 60 days.']

**Jira — SEC-0891 (Created: Feb 3, 2026)**
Summary: CVE-2026-1847 — Critical RCE in auth-service dependency
Priority: Critical | CVSS: 9.8
Timeline: Identified Feb 3 → Patch available Feb 8 → Deployed to staging Feb 19 → Production deploy Mar 1 (26 days)
Comment (@jordan.kim, Feb 15): 'Blocked on staging — change freeze for SOC2 audit prep. Ironic.'
Comment (@priya.v, Feb 20): 'Flagging — we're past 14 days but technically v3.1 was active which gives 30. Proceeding.'

**Slack — #security-reviews (Feb 20, 2026, 11:03 AM)**
@priya.v: Quick gut check — SEC-0891 is at day 17. Under the current policy (v3.1) we have 30 days. But the new policy draft (v4.0) says 14 days. Auditor might apply the stricter standard retroactively since we told them in the readiness assessment that our target is 14 days.
@ciso.williams: We committed to 14 days in the SOC2 description of controls. That's what gets audited regardless of internal policy version.
@priya.v: :grimacing: Got it. So the description of controls is the binding commitment, not the internal policy?
@ciso.williams: Correct. Always has been.
[No further replies]

**Jira — SEC-0923 (Created: Mar 14, 2026)**
Summary: CVE-2026-2190 — Critical SQLi in reporting module
Priority: Critical | CVSS: 9.1
Timeline: Identified Mar 14 → Patch available Mar 16 → Deployed to production Mar 31 (17 days)
Comment (@dev.team.lead, Mar 28): 'WAF rule mitigates exploitation. Compensating control in place since Mar 15.'
No exception ticket filed. No CISO approval documented.

**Jira — SEC-1003 (Created: May 2, 2026)**
Summary: CVE-2026-3021 — Critical deserialization in event-processor
Priority: Critical | CVSS: 9.4
Timeline: Identified May 2 → Remediated May 19 (17 days)
Comment (@priya.v, May 10): 'Over SLA per description of controls. Filing exception.'
Exception approved by CISO in linked ticket SEC-1003-EX.

**Google Drive — /Compliance/SOC2/2026/Description_of_Controls_FINAL.docx (last modified: Jun 2025)**
CC-7.2: 'The Company remediates critical vulnerabilities within 14 days of identification. Compensating controls may be applied when remediation requires extended timelines, subject to CISO approval.'
question: The auditor flagged 3 instances exceeding the 14-day SLA. For the management response, how many of the three represent actual control failures versus exceptions or compliant remediations?

contributor.name: Priya Venkatesh
contributor.title: Information Security & Compliance Manager
contributor.domain_expertise: SOC2, vendor security reviews, data processing agreements, incident disclosure, policy versioning across compliance frameworks

choices: Three failures — all exceeded 14 days and none had compensating controls properly documented per the description of controls

Two failures (SEC-0891 and SEC-0923) — the CISO's Slack message establishes the description of controls as binding, making SEC-0891 non-compliant at 26 days without exception; SEC-1003 had proper exception approval
Zero failures — all three were compliant under internal policy v3.1 (30-day SLA) which was active during Feb and Mar incidents
One failure (SEC-0923, the SQLi vuln) — it had no documented exception or CISO approval; SEC-0891 was under the 30-day internal policy, and SEC-1003 had a proper exception filed
